caption:
Austin’s housing-permit pullback is mostly multifamily.

The Austin–Round Rock–San Marcos metro authorized 18,284 privately owned housing units from January through September 2026, down 10.3% from 20,374 in the same months of 2025.

The split matters:
• Single-family: 11,789 units, down 1.1% from 11,924.
• Multifamily: 6,495 units, down 23.1% from 8,450.

Multifamily here includes structures with two or more units. It accounts for 1,955 of the 2,090 fewer housing units authorized—a calculation from the Census tables.

Why it matters locally: the slowdown in this early measure of future housing supply is much sharper in multifamily than in single-family. Permits measure authorizations; construction starts, completions and future prices require separate evidence.

Opportunity Austin highlighted the overall decline in its November 12 economic update. We checked the underlying Census files directly.

Sources: U.S. Census Bureau, September 2026 and September 2025 Building Permits Survey CBSA tables; Opportunity Austin, November 12, 2026.
